howto.name: Meet the basic requirements
howto.text: Be at least 18 with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.

howto.name: Complete the 63-hour pre-license course
howto.text: Finish Florida's state-approved 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and pass its end-of-course exam.

howto.name: Get fingerprinted
howto.text: Submit electronic fingerprints through a state-approved vendor for your background check.

howto.name: Apply to the DBPR
howto.text: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and receive your exam authorization.

howto.name: Pass the Florida state exam
howto.text: Pass the 100-question Florida sales associate exam (75% or higher) at a Pearson VUE testing center.

howto.name: Activate your license under a broker
howto.text: Join a licensed Florida broker, such as Adams, Cameron & Co., to activate your license and start working.

Holly Hill is a small, working-class city of about 13,300 people, wedged directly between Daytona Beach to the south and Ormond Beach to the north, running along the Halifax River in the heart of Volusia County. Here’s exactly how to get licensed, and what the local market looks like for a new agent.

How do you get a real estate license in Holly Hill?

You earn the Florida real estate sales associate license, valid statewide. There is no separate Holly Hill license. Be 18+ with a high school diploma, complete the 63-hour pre-license course, get fingerprinted, apply to the DBPR, pass the state exam (75% to pass), and activate under a broker. Most people finish in two to four months. Full detail is in our Florida licensing guide.

Is Holly Hill a good market for a new real estate agent?

Yes, in a specific way. Holly Hill isn’t a beach destination in its own right. It’s an affordable, centrally located community sandwiched between two much larger markets, which means buyers priced out of Daytona Beach or Ormond Beach look here for value, and residents who already live here sell and buy again within the same few square miles. That’s steady, referral-driven business, the kind a new agent can build a career on. Across Volusia County, roughly 900 homes sell each month at about a $343,000 median, and Holly Hill’s own price points tend to sit below that county figure, which keeps the buyer pool wide.

Why Holly Hill incorporated as a city, and what it says about the market today

Holly Hill’s origin story is genuinely unusual and tells you something real about who lives here now. The city was founded gradually in the 1870s and 1880s as a farming community along the Halifax River, but it officially became a city on July 1, 1901 for one specific, practical reason: to control livestock. Early residents wanted to keep their razorback hogs fenced in, so they incorporated. The first mayor was Frank “Vet” Cave, a cigar factory owner. That unpretentious, working-class origin isn’t a historical footnote. It shows up now in Holly Hill’s character. This is a no-frills, practical city, not a resort town trying to be something it isn’t. For a new agent, that matters: buyers here are straightforward, looking for value and space, not status. They’re not paying for a brand name. That kind of buyer actually rewards agents who speak directly and deliver results.

The median age factor: an older, established resident base

Holly Hill’s median age is 45 years, meaningfully older than many Florida markets, and that shapes the buying and selling patterns in concrete ways. The city has a substantial population of established retirees and empty-nesters who are either downsizing or settling in for the long term, not moving every three years like younger, more transient populations. That creates a market segment that values stability, knows what it wants, and often buys through referral and word-of-mouth. For a new agent, an older, established resident base means less competition from buyers jumping between houses, but more emphasis on relationships and proving yourself reliable. It also means your repeat-business and referral pipeline, once started, runs steadier and longer than in beach or young-family markets where people churn faster.

Local employers: healthcare and manufacturing keep Holly Hill grounded

Holly Hill is home to Florida Health Care Plans, a major health insurance and healthcare services company headquartered in the city with around 877 employees. Nearby, Metra Electronics Corp. operates a facility here with 301 employees. Across the broader region, Volusia County’s largest employers are healthcare systems like Halifax Health and Florida Hospital Volusia, generating consistent demand for nurses, administrators, and support staff. Unlike markets driven primarily by tourism or seasonal real estate speculation, Holly Hill has a stable, middle-class employment base that generates year-round buyer demand from working professionals and their families. For an agent, that means a more predictable pipeline: employer transfers, healthcare professionals relocating, and families anchored to the community by stable jobs. When someone buys in Holly Hill, they’re often planning to stay, not flip.

Holly Hill sits entirely on the mainland: a geographic advantage

Unlike its immediate neighbors Daytona Beach and Ormond Beach, which span both the barrier island and the mainland, Holly Hill is entirely on the mainland along the Halifax River. That’s not flashy, but it affects everything from property taxes to flood zones to insurance rates to buyer psychology. Mainland properties in central Volusia tend to have lower flood insurance costs than comparable homes on the barrier island, a real financial advantage that matters to practical buyers and to their lenders. Mainland also means no beach-town price markup for water views and proximity to sand, so families get more home for their money. For an agent, this is concrete knowledge that separates you from someone who just recites market statistics. Buyers from the island or from out of state don’t always understand the mainland advantage on their own.

Does the brokerage you start with matter?

More than the town you pick. Your license must be held by a broker, and that brokerage decides your training, tools, and support in the make-or-break first year. A recognized local name carries real weight. Sellers trust it before you say a word.

Why start your real estate career with Adams, Cameron & Co.?

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area’s largest brokerage since 1963, with around 300 agents across Volusia and Flagler County. Holly Hill sits directly between the Daytona Beach headquarters and the Ormond Beach offices, so wherever you are in the city, a full-service Adams, Cameron & Co. office is a short drive either way. New agents get in-house marketing at no cost, seven-day non-competing manager support, structured training, and the global Leading Real Estate Companies of the World referral network.

What is your next step?

Read the licensing guide, go deeper on the town’s real story in our full history of Holly Hill, then start a conversation with Adams, Cameron & Co. No pressure, just a clear picture of the path.
